claims.head: The matchup inside the matchup
claims.body: The Devils are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Golden Knights are the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Devils’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
claims.call: The Devils’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Golden Knights.

claims.head: Hughes gets company tonight
claims.call: The Golden Knights’ L2 (Howden, Karlsson and Holtz) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Devils’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Golden Knights keep sending Karlsson’s line (Howden, Karlsson and Holtz) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Ryan Craig has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Devils’ first line is Gritsyuk, Hughes and Bratt.
claims.nums: At home: 52% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 29% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Ryan Craig likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Devils’ first line.

notes.text: Johnathan Kovacevic was added to the roster on Oct 11 and has played beside Declan Chisholm.
Mitch Marner is away for personal reasons and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Alexander Holtz has taken his spot beside William Karlsson and Brett Howden.

VGK.head: A genuine toss-up
VGK.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Vegas will be without Marner, but they have home-ice advantage. For the Golden Knights, the difference could be keeping dangerous shots away.

NJD.head: Nothing to separate these two
NJD.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Vegas will be without Marner, but they have home-ice advantage. The Devils can tip it if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: The matchup inside the matchup
paras: The Golden Knights are 8-4-0. The Devils have won two in a row.
